# Repository Documentation and Writing Rules

This repository follows the central portfolio standards maintained in [1kmsbrass/rules](https://github.com/1kmsbrass/rules).

## Documentation linking

Canonical rule: [REPO-DOC-001 — Repository Documentation Linking Standard](https://github.com/1kmsbrass/rules/blob/main/rules/repository-work/knowledge-linking-standard.md).

Before creating or substantially updating substantive documentation:

1. Search this repository for existing documents covering the same subject, aliases and related concepts.
2. Reuse or update the authoritative document where appropriate; avoid duplicate sources of truth.
3. Add a **Related Documents** section with direct relative Markdown links to meaningfully related files and a short explanation of each relationship.
4. Consider useful reciprocal links.
5. Verify every relative link and update links when files move or are renamed.

Use standard Markdown links, not Obsidian-only wikilinks as the sole link format. Apply this to documentation, specifications, architecture notes, operational instructions, research and project knowledge. Do not add link noise to source code, generated files, raw data rows or every individual content page. Preserve repository-specific navigation and purpose.

## Personal voice and intellectual influence

Canonical rule: [WRITING-VOICE-001 — Personal Voice and Intellectual Influence](https://github.com/1kmsbrass/rules/blob/main/rules/repository-work/personal-voice-and-intellectual-influence.md).

- Preserve the user's actual point of view, strengths, experiences, preferences, constraints, ambitions and reasoning.
- Personal documents should normally use first person and should sound like the user, not an abstract entrepreneur or detached consultant.
- Do not flatten personal experiences into generic, stoic lessons or make ambitions artificially modest.
- Use analytical depth, clear distinctions and meaningful terminology while preserving the user's natural metaphors and personality.
- The user values selected concepts associated with Jordan B. Peterson. Use these only where they genuinely clarify an idea; do not imitate his exact voice or force his terminology into every document.
- Before deliberately applying or attributing Peterson's concepts, consult the [Jordan B. Peterson — Checked Concept Reference](https://github.com/1kmsbrass/rules/blob/main/references/jordan-b-peterson.md). Verify precise attributions against the original book, lecture or official source. Separate Peterson's idea, our interpretation and the user's own position.
- Technical, legal, financial, safety and customer-facing documents must prioritise accuracy, compliance and audience clarity.

## Local conventions and precedence

Follow the central standards alongside this repository's more specific architecture, product, data, privacy, brand and audience rules. A more specific rule governs its own subject where applicable. If a conflict is genuine, identify it rather than silently guessing.

The central rules repository is the authoritative source. This file is a local pointer and working reminder, not a copied source of truth.

## Completion check

Before considering a substantive documentation change complete, verify that:
- Existing related files were searched.
- Duplicate explanations were avoided or reconciled.
- Related Documents links were added and checked.
- The user's point of view and relevant context were preserved where applicable.
- Peterson concepts, if used, were checked and attributed accurately.
- Repository-specific requirements were respected.
